about.title: About me
about.p1: I'm Renato Decker. I've spent over 20 years managing projects in environments where stopping is not an option — 24/7 industrial operations, teams of up to 20 people, complex system integrations, and clients at vastly different levels of maturity.
about.p2: I'm not the consultant who delivers a methodology deck and disappears. I stay through go-live. I adjust the plan when scope changes in week five. I negotiate between stakeholders with conflicting goals. And I make knowledge transfer real — to the client, to their team, to whoever will keep the system running.
about.p3: Method matters. But what actually delivers results is pragmatism, adaptability, and an unrelenting focus on what truly matters to the business.

c1.challenge: Implementation in an industrial slaughterhouse running 24/7 — zero tolerance for downtime. Integration of shop floor, WMS, shipping, and quality with existing production systems. Scope under constant adjustment due to client-required customizations.
c1.result: Delivered on time. 20% reduction in data entry rework. Integrated inventory and shipping with real-time visibility across the entire operation.

c2.challenge: Integration of an ERP — with heavily customized commercial policies — into a B2B platform built by a third party. No prior experience with this type of integration. Client's online processes undefined at project start.
c2.result: After three distinct technical approaches, a hybrid sync/async model was built from scratch. Go-live completed with full data integrity and commercial policies working correctly online.

c3.challenge: Full back-office and production implementation with a client team smaller than typical for this scale. All training was directed to a third-party consulting firm contracted by the client to operate the system — no qualified internal team to receive knowledge directly.
c3.result: Delivered on time and within budget. Consulting firm fully trained to operate all modules and provide independent support to the client.

philosophy.title: Leadership Philosophy
philosophy.p1: Project management isn't about following a framework — it's about reading the environment, adapting the approach, and keeping the team focused on the right outcome regardless of what changes along the way. Method matters. But methodological rigidity in the field creates more problems than it solves.
philosophy.p2: Real stakeholder management is communication with courage: not just reporting what's on the schedule, but naming what's at risk before it becomes a crisis. That requires building technical and managerial credibility simultaneously — and maintaining it when pressure rises.
philosophy.p3: Governance isn't bureaucracy. It's the set of rituals, artifacts, and decisions that keep a portfolio readable for those who make the calls. A PMO that produces documentation without removing obstacles doesn't govern — it files. The difference lies in the willingness to have hard conversations and act on what the data shows.
